region.text: the March of Styria raised to a duchy; no boundary on the page

ledger.note: 1180: Frederick Barbarossa raises the March of Styria to a duchy. 'created by Emperor Frederick Barbarossa in 1180 when he raised the March of Styria to a duchy', 'to a duchy of equal rank with neighbouring Carinthia and Bavaria'; infobox 'Raised to duchy by Frederick Barbarossa: 1180'. The page gives the march, not a boundary. In 1186 Ottokar IV 'signed the Georgenberg Pact with the mighty House of Babenberg', 'after which both duchies should in perpetuity be ruled in personal union' (Austria and Styria).

1192: Ottokar IV dies and Styria passes to the Babenberg Duke of Austria, Leopold V, under the 1186 Georgenberg Pact. 'Upon his death in 1192, Styria as stipulated fell to the Babenberg Leopold V'. The Ottokar II page: Styria 'since 1192 had been ruled in personal union with Austria'.

1254: Styria passes to the Hungarian crown after the Babenberg line ends. 'The Austrian Babenbergs became extinct in 1246' (Duke Frederick II 'was killed in battle against King Bela IV of Hungary'); 'It passed quickly through the hands of Hungarian kings in 1254'. The ruler list has Bela IV 1254-1258 and Stephen V 1258-1260 against Ottokar II.

July 1260: Ottokar II of Bohemia wins Styria at Kressenbrunn. 'Ottokar defeated the Hungarians in July 1260 at the Battle of Kressenbrunn, ending years of disputes over Styria with Bela IV'; 'Bela now ceded Styria back to Ottokar'; lead: 'Duke of Styria from 1260'. The Duchy page (1260 Kressenbrunn) agrees. Styria is held in personal union with Bohemia; Cliopatria draws the land inside its Kingdom of Bohemia 1260-1278.

November 1276: Ottokar II gives up Styria; the Habsburgs follow. 'This compelled Premysl Ottokar in November 1276 to sign a new treaty by which he gave up all claims to Austria and the neighboring duchies, retaining for himself only Bohemia and Moravia' (Styria is my reading of 'neighboring duchies'). The Duchy page's infobox says 'To Habsburg Austria: 1276/78', its ruler list has Rudolph I from 1278 ('The House of Habsburg provided Styria with dukes of their lineage from that point on'), and Ottokar fell at the Marchfeld on 26 August 1278; Cliopatria moves the land from Bohemia to the House of Habsburg in 1279.

1379: the Treaty of Neuberg divides the Habsburg lands and Styria becomes the core of Inner Austria. Styria was 'separated from Austria by the 1379 Treaty of Neuberg', 'after which Styria, Carinthia, and Carniola formed the Inner Austrian territory' under the Leopoldian line, who made Graz their residence. An association of duchies, not territory of its own: no gain or loss is entered.

region.text: 'the comital Celje estates in Lower Styria'; the page gives no boundary for the estates, Lower Styria is approximated by a 45 km radius round Maribor plus Celje

ledger.note: 1456: the Counts of Celje die out and their Lower Styrian estates enlarge Styria. 'In 1456 they could significantly enlarge the Styrian territory ... by acquisition and re-acquisition of the comital Celje estates in Lower Styria'. Counts of Celje page: Ulrich II was assassinated in Belgrade 'on 8 November' 1456, 'the male line of the Counts of Cilli died out', and 'all of their estates and property were handed over to the Habsburgs on the basis of the inheritance agreement' of 1443; the same page also says 'In 1458 the county is annexed to Austria', and the Matthias Corvinus page gives 9 November for Ulrich's death. The Celje estates also lay in Carinthia and Carniola ('large estates in the adjoining duchies of Styria and Carinthia'); only the Lower Styrian part is drawn here.
1457: Styria and Austria are again in one hand. 'Both duchies were again ruled in personal union, when Leopold's grandson Frederick V inherited Austria in 1457.'

1564: a second Inner Austrian Habsburg branch takes Styria. 'A second Inner Austrian cadet branch of the Habsburgs ruled over Styria from 1564' (Archduke Charles II; Graz 'a centre of the Counter-Reformation').
1619: Ferdinand II, Archduke of Inner Austria, 'became sole rule of all Habsburg hereditary lands and Holy Roman Emperor in 1619'; the Inner Austrian line ends in the common Habsburg rule.
1804: 'Styria remained a part of the Habsburg monarchy and from 1804 belonged to the Austrian Empire.'
1867: in the Compromise 'the duchy was assigned as a crown land for the Cisleithanian part of Austria-Hungary' (infobox status 'Kronland of Cisleithanian Austria').

region.text: the duchy at its end: 'a Cisleithanian crown land of Austria-Hungary until its dissolution in 1918'

ledger.note: October 1918: Austria-Hungary dissolves and with it the crown land. Infobox 'Austria-Hungary dissolved: 31 October 1918' and 'Collapse of German Austria: 10 September 1919'. 'The Slovene Lower Styrian part joined the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs'; 'the southern third of Lower Styria with Maribor' passed to the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes (no year inside 1918-1919 on the page); the rest became Austrian Styria. The duchy's own end is the page's inference from the dissolution, hence confidence 2.

wars.name: Battle of Kressenbrunn

zones.text: Styria, the object of 'years of disputes over Styria with Bela IV'

wars.outcome: Ottokar II defeated the Hungarians in July 1260 at Kressenbrunn; Bela IV ceded Styria back to Ottokar and the peace was sealed by a royal marriage; Richard of Cornwall recognised his claim.
wars.note: The start of the fighting is undated on the page ('years of disputes'); the papal mediation by which Ottokar 'would yield large parts of Styria to Bela' is also undated. No contest zone is entered: the pages give no campaign on Styrian ground.

wars.name: Austrian-Hungarian War (1477-1488)
wars.outcome: Matthias Corvinus 'conquered most of the Lower Austrian territories' (Siege of Vienna 1485, Wiener Neustadt captured 1487); after his death on 6 April 1490 Frederick regained the Austrian lands 'without serious fight' and Maximilian I signed the Peace of Pressburg in 1491, which returned Matthias' conquests.
wars.note: The page does not mention Styria; after the fall of Wiener Neustadt in 1487 'Frederick fled to Graz'. The Matthias Corvinus page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthias_Corvinus) has him in 1479 take 'the fortresses of the Archbishopric in Carinthia, Carniola and Styria' and in 1481 seize 'the town of Mautern in Styria and Sankt Poelten in Lower Austria'. Cliopatria's Kingdom of Hungary shape for 1487-1491 contains all of modern Styria (67 cells) and its House of Habsburg shape drops it; neither page supports a full Hungarian occupation of the duchy (Graz was the emperor's refuge in 1487), so no zone and no contest or occupation event is entered. Gap for a gap-filler (notes).

certainty.note: The pages opened give no boundary line for the duchy at any date; the outline is modern Steiermark plus Lower Styria after 1456. No treaty or survey line is on the pages, so the whole life is soft.

notes:
Cliopatria's five 'Duchy of Styria' shapes are not Styria. (1) 1260-1271, 16,888 km2, bbox 10.23-13.38E 46.10-47.59N: by the gazetteer 62 of 67 cells lie in Tyrol, 3 in Carinthia, none in Steiermark (13.65-16.10E, 46.72-47.77N). The area equals modern Steiermark's (16,944 km2) but the position is about 3 degrees of longitude west; it may be a Tyrolean outline (a county-of-tyrol dossier is needed in any case). (2) 1272-1421 and 1422-1449: one Friulian cell (Udine province, about 190 km WSW of Graz), inside Cliopatria's Patriarchate of Aquileia outline. (3) 1450-1496 and 1497-1501: 8 cells (about 2,000 km2) in the Gorizia-Tolmin-Kobarid-Udine borderland, with a bbox identical to the Patriarchate of Aquileia's 1422-1449 outline (the Aquileia row ends 1449, this one starts 1450); probably the Aquileian remnant relabelled. All five are verdict wrong; the page names no Friulian or Tyrolean possession.

Where Styria's real land sits in Cliopatria: Kingdom of Bohemia 1260-1278 (62 cells of Steiermark, 66 from 1272), House of Habsburg 1279-1486 (64-66 cells), Kingdom of Hungary 1487-1491 (all 67 cells; House of Habsburg has 0), House of Habsburg 1492-1515, Habsburg Monarchy (0 cells in 1490 and 1500, 66 in 1520, 67 in 1600). The orchestrator must decide how to render this dossier against those rows. This dossier treats the duchy as a state in its own right 1180-1918 (the page's infobox: raised 1180, dissolved with Austria-Hungary in 1918) held by changing dynasties in personal union, recorded as rename events (rule 2); the bohemia, house-of-habsburg and habsburg-monarchy dossiers (other parts of eu-09) should treat Styria as a union partner or vassal tint rather than draw it twice. If the project prefers Cliopatria's partition, keep this dossier only for 1180-1259 and for its ledger/captions and drop its shapes after 1260.

Life span: Cliopatria's row is 1260-1501, the page's duchy is 1180-1918. I used the page. The 1502-1918 stretch rests on one page (no territorial change is dated on it except the 1918-19 loss of the southern third of Lower Styria) and can be cut at 1806 if the orchestrator wants the duchy to end with the Empire; a dissolve event at 1501 would have been invented, so none is written.

Not settled (page silent or budget spent, 5 pages): (a) whether any part of Lower Styria (Maribor, Ptuj, Celje) belonged to the duchy before 1456: the page says only 'northern Slovenia' and 'acquisition and re-acquisition of the comital Celje estates in Lower Styria'; the base outline is Steiermark only before 1456 and a gap-filler should open 'Styria' or 'March of Styria'. (b) The Hungarian seizures of the 1480s: Cliopatria draws Hungary over all of Styria in 1487-1491; the two pages opened say Frederick fled to Graz in 1487 and name only Mautern (1481) and the Archbishopric's fortresses (1479). No event entered. (c) The 1254 transfer is dated by the Duchy page only ('in 1254'); the Ottokar II page has an undated papal mediation under which Ottokar 'would yield large parts of Styria to Bela'. The Ennstal and other border parcels are not placed. (d) 1276 against 1278: the Ottokar II page gives November 1276 for the renunciation; the Duchy page gives 'To Habsburg Austria: 1276/78' and Rudolph I from 1278; the ruler strip follows the page (1278), the ledger the treaty (1276), Cliopatria moves the land at 1279. (e) Ulrich II of Celje died on 8 November 1456 on the Celje page and on 9 November on the Matthias Corvinus page; the Celje page also says the county was annexed in 1458. (f) The 1512 entry of the duchy into the Austrian Circle is a Reichskreis membership, not territory, and has no event. (g) Ruler list: read from the page through a WebFetch extract that ends at Ferdinand II (1637); later dukes are not recorded.

Counterparts needing dossiers: march-of-styria (970-1180, the predecessor), county-of-celje (the Counts of Celje, comital 1341, princes 1436, extinct 1456), county-of-tyrol (Cliopatria lacks it; possible source of the 1260 outline). Habsburg rows are eu-09 (house-of-habsburg, habsburg-monarchy) and Patriarchate of Aquileia is eu-13.

Gazetteer: 'Lower Styria' (region; Slovene Styria, Maribor-Celje-Ptuj) is missing and was replaced by a 45 km radius round Maribor plus the Celje municipality; 'Celje' has no place entry (only an admin1 municipality). Neither is unknown to the validator.
